objective: Route the Android public Community Wall first-view BannerAd fallback through its dedicated community-entry unit instead of silently using the general Community feed banner unit.
productionBaselineEvidence: Main includes the merged Android NativeAd-first first-view renderer. Production telemetry for build 28 shows public_wall_entry no-fill and other failures, but current installed OTA has not been verified to include the merged first-view implementation. The existing getBuklodBannerUnitId mapping already supports EXPO_PUBLIC_ADMOB_COMMUNITY_ENTRY_BANNER_UNIT_ID; the Android NativeAd-first wrapper currently derives 'community' for all public Wall surfaces and bypasses that dedicated mapping.
chosenApproach: Pass an explicit banner placement override only for the public community_entry first-view. Keep the NativeAd primary request, stable placement ID, shared request reservation, route/consent checks, and all Organization/Cluster feed mappings unchanged. Fall back to the existing general Community banner when the dedicated entry unit is not configured.
selectionRationale: Use the existing intended unit-selection mapping with no new IDs, SDK calls, or requests. This corrects a deterministic Android wrapper mismatch while preserving existing fallback compatibility.
alternativeApproaches: Leave all public Wall entry fallbacks on the Community feed banner; rejected because it bypasses the already-supported dedicated community-entry unit.
Create a new AdMob unit or change remote placement flags; rejected because an existing unit configuration hook is already present and external inventory setup is not verified.
Use a placement override only for community_entry and preserve all other scope mappings; selected.
preserveBehaviors: NativeAd remains the first request and BannerAd remains sequential fallback.
No concurrent duplicate ad requests or changes to shared cooldown.
UMP consent, SDK readiness, network, foreground, route safety, remote placement kill switches and PG content rating remain authoritative.
Organization and Cluster Wall banner units remain scope-specific.
No changes to native package, runtime, AdMob app ID, database, or production OTA workflow.
acceptanceChecks: Public community_entry first-view passes community_entry to the BannerAd unit selector.
If the dedicated community-entry banner unit is absent, the selector retains the existing Community banner fallback.
NativeAd-first request identity and stable public_wall_entry placement ID remain unchanged.
Organization and Cluster first-view banner mappings remain org_community and cluster_community.
Focused Wall/ad regression test, Engineering Accountability, Performance R1 QA and Main integration QA pass.
No production OTA is published by this change.
